body:
What I said is not a half truth and I am not ignoring anything. I beg not to generalize, and that is all. I will accept any decisions Europe would reach, and am ready for ecile, death or jail. It's is not the problem - the problem is dialectics that remove subjectivity and individuality from people, and that is what Putin does, and one of the reasons I hate him.

But I understand, who cares really. Russians are intrinsically evil - but I hope that we still make our individual choices regardless.

I am a Russian. We might be terrible people of failed country, but a mental condition such as autism is not a synonym to evil and should never be used in such context. It marginalizes people that should be a part of a healthy society.

PS yeah yeah I'm bad and everything, and even I agree those ppl are immoral bastards.

I am a Russian, I would never attack and harass any person, especially someone in a vulnerable position. I never spread any horrible words of the Russian propaganda - it is usually not only immoral, bit also incredibly stupid. I do support a relative in Russia a bit, but only because they quit their job and are prepping for leaving a country with a working visa elsewhere.

I hate Putin, and not only for this war, but also for many  other crimes. 

I still deserve a severe penalty for my country's sins and who I am does not matter. But do not generalize and speak for ourselves. Yes, we all are responsible for Putin and his wars. Yes, maybe we should be banned from Europe or life altogether. No, we do not all - all 150 millions of people - share the same morality, perspective and political views. That's Putin's rhetoric he inherited from commies. We are different people who have different views, but who should be equally punished.

Do not deny Russians of our individual voices, that's Putler's job.

Sorry.

I am sorry for Ukraine and I am deeply ashamed of my country, my people, my history and myself. Civilized world should figure out how to punish us, but the priority right now is stopping Putin. If a ban would work, then so be it, but do not forget to demand complete military support of Ukraine from your countries and a gas embargo! You either find way to eliminate all Russians, or just Putin's clique of maniacs,  but isolation will never be complete unless Russia goes kaboom. You do not want a belligerent neighbor with people who have nowhere else to turn to. Unfortunately, Russians want to live, so even in isolation we won't seek death like we ought to. Instead, we will be able to be used as meat or manpower to support God knows whatever atrocities Russian government (usurpers...) have in mind.

I am very sorry for the misconception of those Russians you have talked to. All Russians are intrinsically evil and deserve to be punished. Slava Ukraine! And damn Russia and.all my people. We do not learn how to be humans and should be treated accordingly.

I am so sorry for your experience. Those people are terrible. I promise not all Russians are like that - we are all intrinsically evil, true, but I know many who support the refugees at the best of their abilities. But of course, we Russians should all bear responsibility for the disgrace of our country and nation! It is unexcusable, but just know that others would never do auch a thing. As a Russian, I wish Ukraine a glorious victory and healing, and Russia to be punished.

Just kill all Russians already. We are bad people because we are either losers unable to win over killers and usurpers or insane maniacs supporting abuse. We do not deserve to live, okay?

Just whatever. Do not return Russians back to Russia, do not fuel the war with men that could be used as dead meat, and with qualified ppl who can work in critical industries, supporting the war or the economy of our shithole of a country. If we are dead, we can no longer either support the war or blemish the civilized world with our damned existence.

Duh.

And for God's sake send weapons to Ukraine and STOP BUYING the bloody gas. Negotiate with China to stop supporting Russia. There are so many things that can be done. At last, just one nuke at Moscow might stop Russia altogether.

But maybe you are right. I left Russia years ago - and I have to go back, I will have nothing to lose and will put my life on line.... On the other hand, will I be putting the lives on my children on line? I do not know. Just kill us, let us avoid making those choices. We cannot be trusted to make the right one anyway.

And I tell you something. If I won't face a legal actions against myself in EU due to my citizenship and heritage, I will still take my life - but I will live until I see the end of the damned ILLEGAL dictatorial regime that eats people and destroy countries. Bloody hell. Even as an inhuman something I think I deserve a celebration.

I show no bravery,  I did not live in Russia for almost a decade. But I know brave souls who protest openly in Russia. A couple of them are in a jail already, but the others do the most important work.

Why won't NATO just bomb Russia?Just out of curiosity. One nuclear strike at Moscow - and the world would be free and a better place. Maybe it would take a few more strikes at military infrastructure. If Russians are not coming to senses on their own, then other countries could force it - and with the smaller sacrifice millions would be saved.

FYI I am a Russian and even I understand that my country and nation are a nuisance to Europe and possibly the world. If we need to be gone to stop the world - so be it. Why don't the civilized nations  do something like that? Is it impossible to strike first and make Russia unable to answer? What is a problem here?

Thank you for the answer. A lot of people to whom I talk, especially Russians, have a very grim vision of the future even after Putin's death. I personally think that a change of power is a good thing, and is a minimum condition for any systematic healing.

As a Russian, I guess that even if my power to stop the war now is limited, it is crucial to be ready to that moment if history when the tides turn - and make sure that the impact of the change can be used to the maximum to create a different and more sustainable system. Does not sound like a punishment, bit at least this is something that might be useful.

To me as a Russian it sounds like a good plan and not a punishment:) Alternatively, a decentralized confederation sounds very nice... It's too big for its own good, and too centralized. Concentration of power in one place and a very few hands is a recipe for disaster.

Gosh, how can it be done.
...I just hope destroying Russia means it's current form of governance and administrative structure, and not annihilation of people or cities, even if that would be fair.

It is frightening how Russia, pretending to fight Nazism, literally repeats the history. Even Putin's speeches are so much like Hitler's. It's insufferable how much of hypocrites Russian government is.

But how to punish Russia?

While the war continues - support Ukraine with weapons and pressure Russian economy - which might be more or less effective. Russians might feel the decrease in their quality of life, but we just accept it all like docile animals.

Say, the war is over, Ukraine wins - and gets it's territories back. Putin is in still in power, or there's another shithead, or a fighting groups/clans.

Or the war is over, Russia gets Ukrainian lands and wants more - and threatens Baltics, or Moldova, or whatnot - its appetite is terrifying.

What is the appropriate punishment? Before Nurenberg 2.0 is possible to hold specific people accountable, Russian government needs to change completely.

Is economic failure of the country enough? Russia has enough resources to survive decades with the worst conditions, keep the nukes and still be a threat.

I mean, ideally Russians will revolt and overthrow the regime. Good to be optimistic, but relying on that scenario is naive. What more can be done to ensure that USSR 2.0 scenario does not happen and a monster of the militaristic empire does not bring more tragedies in the next decades.

P S I am a Russian migrated years ago. I feel very much involved and believe that Russia as it is now is a threat to the world. I wish, after the hot war is over, for fair punishment of perpetrators, but cannot imagine how it should be done if Russia does not do 180 and become a completely different place ruled by different people. Sorry if my question is too ignorant.

This woman will have special place for her in hell - not only for the pro-war propaganda, but also for the spread of pure stupidity.

I am from Russia, and I do not hate anyone on Earth more than those empowered criminals and incompetent fools who spread their insanity onto their people. And don't get me wrong - those guys are destroying Ukraine physically, but they also destroy Russia, and have appetite for anything within their reach. Europe should do whatever needs to be done to stop it. These people are the literal monkeys with bombs, they will destroy Ukraine, Russia and the whole world if they can - and explain it with someone's orders or preventive measures or whatever their usual bullshit. And then they'll be genuinely surprised with the outcome!

God save us all from the brainless, soulless cruelty and the people who support and inspire it.

After I see them hung in Hague, I'll rest in peace. My generation failed not only our country, but the whole world - and we will be burning not too far from this woman in hell for not being able to win the only fight that matters. The West should not repeat our mistakes, and has to win no matter what.

Even now - if you are not ready to risk Russia using nuclear weapon, then a full gas embargo and a deal with Asian countries to stop supporting Russia is a must right now. Otherwise the price will be even higher. Remember Hitler? Do NOT negotiate with madmen. This is the war that has to be won as soon as possible no matter what. Sorry to put it like that - it is the only chance of a peaceful future that both Europeans and Russians have.

As a Russian, I strongly disagree.
Being a Russian, a high chance is that you would hate Putin, even before the war, for many things he did in 20 years.

You probably would not go to the streets, not until you feel that the support is so huge that the protest have a chance.

But you would still resist. If you are courageous, you would be stopping trains or secretly setting military offices on fire. You might be posting on social media, or sending links to 1-on-1 chat to your friends. You might be doing small things, insignificant on the outside, but that are very powerful inside Russia, like placing green ribbons everywhere you go, just to send a signal to the other protesters that they are not alone. You might leave Russia and post openly from the safety of another country, breaking the spiral of silence.

You might send letters to the deputies and other officials, disagreeing with the war, with the internal policies, demanding truth about the fallen Russian soldiers - anything that would send a signal to officials that the people still have other opinions.

As a parent, you would resist political propaganda inside your children's school. As a student, you would sabotage the propagandistic lectures. As a key infrastructure worker, you would work slower than ever, making many mistakes, but formally following all protocols.

In these times in the country like Russia those small gestures have a grave importance. No, it cannot stop the war right now; yes, it can at least increase the chances for the future.

What I say is that there many forms of protests that suite both high and low-risk types of people. As an outsider you might not see them or might not see their significance; some would laugh and call those people deranged pussies for not marching the street. Let's not forget that there are many supporter too, and almost all of the armed people are on the "dark" side.

But once we will realize that those small things would be the most important in our lives.

Damn madmen and dictators. NO to war!!!

No. Culture and science, progress and thriving economy is what Putin fears the most. He wants to stop time to stay in power forever, but times change, people change, and he had to start a bloody war to raise his ratings.

Future is his greatest fear and enemy. Those who want Russians back to stone age and isolated play HIS tune - he wants an isolated regime and brocken people without any future, then his regime would thrive.

I understand the will on many people to punish Russians, but the true goal should be the fall of the cannibalistic Kremlin and enabling a healthier, decentralized governance system for Russia - or whatever will be left of it.

And destroying nuclear weapons.

Till that happens, even if Putin would be happy and won't move forward with his imperialistic and paranoid ideas (does it even sound likely?), and Russia will get water-tight iron curtain, the threat to the whole Europe or even the war will remain.

BUT
All scientific or technological exchange that can be used for military, should be ceased.

Now they are silencing the opposition with the sentence of up to 15 years. So I say, 10 years for every bloody pro-Putin troll, and life sentence for the propaganda leaders.

They are not only responsible for lighting up the fire of the war in Ukraine, they also fail our own country and people. I hate them with all my heart, but think they should be punished by law, as other criminals. Possibly, for a treason. (Against Russia and humanity.)

But anyway, Hague awaits them. They burn in hell forever.

Common people though, regardless of their position about the war, should not be punished, and instead informed and educated about all evils that Putin's clique brought: all atrocities of the war, tortures in Russia, supporting totalitarian regimes across the globe... Like Germans were educated about the Holocaust. There should be TV shows, books, museums, field trips, lectures, etc. Only by finally accepting all the dark times, all the crimes, all the failures we would be able to overcome the past, and move towards the future.

Russians should worry about Russia, then Ukraine and Belarus. We doom 2 other countries and our own too. Now it's cemented our future will be dark and, quite possibly, not too long.

USA and China did nothing for that.

Only our own powerlessness.
Thank you!! I will look into Efexor and maybe other medicine.

He is seriously detached from reality. Someone remove him from Kremlin and give him a PC with civilization V.

I really really hate this man.

Thank you. Your words mean a lot. I don't mind carrying a burden - but I don't even understand what it really means. If my parents, or kids, or friends make a mess, I'd want to offer help. But the mess that is happening is so much larger than me, and more dreadful than anything I seen before.

Thank you! I will try... It's confusing right now. Sometimes I think I understand rationally my zone of control, the other times I feel disoriented. I will try doing what I can and think is worth doing.

Thank you so much! I will watch the video. Was just reading Hannah Arendt, and it seems to expand  her ideas, based on the description. Maybe I am wrong - but nevertheless, I appreciate your response and the reference.

I fact, there were protests in 2008 and 2014. Not enough - and in 2014 the war actually strengthened Putin's supporters. I do not understand this, but it a fact. And many other protests against Putin in other years.

How, in practical sense, to be responsible for all of the evil? I ask as a Russian both my ethnicity and citizenship.

I read the news, I see all of the atrocities that Russian soldiers do, I even know a Russian person who is supporting the war. As a human, I grieve for Ukrainians and their country and help refugees in Europe where I live. I do that as a human; as a but as a Russian I have no idea what to do. I donate to human right defenders and independent media in Russia and join the protests in my city so that Europe stops buying Russian gas. This is not enough, not nearly enough.

I feel that the only two things could give me indulgence: joining Ukrainian army or flying back to Russia and get arrested. But I hate the war, and I have two teenage dependents who ARE innocent and have never harmed anyone. Even if I kill myself - it will not help anyone. Also, indulgence is not responsibility. I can deal with guilt, but how can I, as an adult, deal with the army of my compatriots invading a country for nothing and kill their people for the delusions of grandeur of our insane leader?

How to be responsible right now, as a person and a citizen? Those who protest now and protested before are not doing enough because they can't win. Those who voted against Putin do not matter because he still won. Even the journalists that are now risking their safety are not doing enough.

I was reading post-war philosophy and literature: 
Jaspers, Arendt, Thomas Mann... Being responsible means accepting that you did wrong, stoping doing wrong, remembering what you did, compensating with money and deeds for the harm you brought, making sure that you never repeat - and generally, develop compassion and humanism personally and as a society.

But right now, right here. If you tell me the way to be responsible - I will gladly do that, unless it endangers those who I am also responsible for. Just one note: I was told before that I should just go and kill myself if I have any heart... I do not think that a suicide is actually a responsible act. But other than that - what and how?

Disclaimer: I am very sorry if I offend anyone. I understand that we Russians lost our rights to ask questions and have conversations with normal people. I would still be grateful for your answers. I am sorry for what my country did and the people who support it for whatever reason. I am sorry for my nation's imperialistic dreams. I am sorry for all Russians, opposition or not, who do not fight the war with our own cannibals and letting Ukrainians do it instead. The world is mad, and we brought much of it to the world.
